questions.q: Successful completion of a major design project depends on a student making the correct link between
options: action and time management.
sustainability and appropriateness of materials.
experimentation and development of practical skills.
generation of concept designs and organising materials.
questions.explanation: Completing a major project on time relies on linking the action plan to the time plan so tasks are sequenced and scheduled realistically. This is the 'ATF' management spine of phase one (action, time, finance). The other pairings matter but do not directly determine whether the whole project is completed.

questions.q: Identify the correct sequence of the three phases of the major design project (MDP).
options: Project evaluation; project development and realisation; project proposal and management
Project proposal and project management; project development and realisation; project evaluation
Project development and realisation; project proposal and management; project evaluation
Project proposal and management; project evaluation; project development and realisation
questions.explanation: The three phases run as DRIPER at full scale: phase one proposes and plans (Define plus action/time/finance), phase two develops and realises (Research, Ideate, Produce), and phase three evaluates (Evaluate, Refine). Any other order breaks the design-process logic of defining a need before solving it.

questions.q:
A design team is about to start developing a new range of products. Part of this process is the implementation of management plans.

These plans ensure that the products
options: meet the intended purpose.
address all legal requirements.
are developed on time and on budget.
meet the needs of the target market.
questions.explanation: Management plans — action, time and finance plans (ATF) — sequence tasks and allocate resources so the product is delivered on schedule and within budget. Meeting purpose, legal needs and the target market are achieved through other parts of the design process.

questions.q: On what basis is the major design project marked?
options: On the quality and appearance of the final product alone
On the folio and the project together, with the folio rewarding documented evidence of the design process
On the folio alone, regardless of the finished product
On the number of pages and neatness of the folio
questions.explanation: The MDP is marked on the folio and the project together, and the folio rewards evidence of process, not just a pretty final product. A beautiful object with a thin folio scores poorly; a solid object whose folio shows rigorous research, justified decisions and continual evaluation scores well.

questions.q: Why do designers establish and review 'criteria to evaluate success' when designing?
options: To increase the number of sales of a product
To ensure environmental factors are considered
To ensure the final design meets the specified needs
To maintain product awareness for further refinement of innovative products
questions.explanation: Criteria to evaluate success are measurable benchmarks set in the project proposal (the 'C' of NICe) and used to check the final design meets the specified needs. The other options are narrower commercial or environmental concerns, not the overall purpose of evaluation criteria.

questions.q: Which response to a design decision in a folio or exam answer reaches the top marking band?
options: Narrating: listing the steps taken, e.g. 'I chose pine, then I cut the legs, then I sanded it.'
Justifying: stating the decision, the reason, the relevant factor and the supporting evidence
Describing the final appearance of the finished product in detail
Listing every material considered, without giving reasons
questions.explanation: Narrating only describes what you did and caps low because anyone can list steps. Justifying explains why, tying the decision to a factor affecting design and to evidence such as a test result, which is what the markers reward. The pattern that scores is decision, reason, factor, evidence.

questions.q: From memory: what is the difference between narrating and justifying a design decision, and which one scores?
keyPoints: Narrating describes what you did — the steps you took — and caps your marks low, because anyone can list steps.
Justifying explains why each decision was made, with reasons tied to the factors affecting design and supported by evidence such as research or test results — and this scores, reaching the top band.
The pattern that scores is: decision, reason, factor, evidence.
questions.explanation: If you recalled that justifying (why, with factor + evidence) outscores narrating (what), and named the decision-reason-factor-evidence pattern, grade yourself Good or Easy.

questions.q: Recall the three mnemonics that form the spine of module H1, and state what each stands for.
keyPoints: DRIPER — the design process: Define, Research, Ideate, Produce, Evaluate, Refine.
NICe — what the project proposal must contain: the Need, the areas of Investigation, and the Criteria to evaluate success.
ATF — the management plans: Action, Time and Finance.
questions.explanation: DRIPER for the process, NICe for the proposal, ATF for the management. If you produced all three with their expansions, mark it Good or Easy.

questions.q: Describe how action plans and ongoing evaluation processes work together to contribute to the development of a successful design.
questions.modelAnswer: As part of the design process the designer develops an action plan to organise an appropriate and efficient operation, sequencing tasks correctly so the project runs efficiently. Combined with an ongoing evaluation structure, this helps ensure a successful design: if ongoing evaluation is not carried out, development may fail to address concerns about important design factors such as function, cost or safety. Together, action plans and ongoing evaluation ensure the end product best meets the needs of the client and the consumer.

criteria.descriptor: Provides characteristics and features of how action plans AND ongoing evaluation processes work together to contribute to a successful design
Provides characteristics and features of how action plans AND/OR evaluation processes contribute to a successful design
Sketches in general terms how action plans AND/OR evaluation processes contribute to a successful design, OR identifies a feature of action plans AND a feature of evaluation processes
Identifies a feature of action plans OR evaluation processes

questions.explanation: Link the action plan (sequencing and scheduling tasks) to continual evaluation against the criteria — the two together drive the project toward a solution that meets the need, which is exactly what the folio must evidence.

questions.q: 'Evidence of process beats a pretty product.' Justify this statement with reference to how the major design project is marked and to the role of the folio.
questions.modelAnswer: The major design project is marked on the folio and the project together, not on the finished product alone, so a high-quality outcome with a thin folio scores poorly while a solid outcome with a rigorous folio scores well. The folio is the documented evidence of the entire design process — research, sketches, decisions, tests, management plans and evaluation — and the marking guidelines reward this evidence of process. A strong folio justifies each significant decision using the pattern decision, reason, factor, evidence, links choices to the eleven factors affecting design, and shows continual evaluation against the criteria. Because the folio must be compiled throughout the project, it demonstrates a genuine, dated, evidence-based process that cannot be reconstructed from memory at the end. Therefore documented, justified process evidence earns the higher bands, justifying the claim that evidence of process beats a pretty product.

criteria.descriptor: Justifies the statement thoroughly, explaining that the MDP is marked on folio and project together and that the folio's documented, justified evidence of process is what the marking rewards
Explains how the folio documents the design process and contributes to the marks, with some reference to justification or continual evaluation
Identifies that the folio records the process and/or that the MDP is marked on more than the final product

questions.explanation: Top-band answers connect the marking basis (folio + project together) to the folio's purpose (evidence of process) and to the justify-don't-narrate meta-skill (decision, reason, factor, evidence) plus documenting throughout.
